stories.headline: LDC graduation window extended to 2029, but reforms cannot wait, columnist argues
stories.summary: Columnist Fahmida Khatun argues the UN General Assembly's 29 October decision giving Bangladesh three more years - graduation now 24 November 2029 instead of 24 November 2026 - buys vital time but cannot fix structural weakness alone. She argues Bangladesh met the CDP's GNI, HAI and EVI tests in 2018 and 2021, yet must now cut power, transport and customs costs, widen exports and settle post-graduation tariffs and rules of origin with partners, since duty-free access alone will not keep it competitive.
stories.why_it_matters: LDC graduation is a core BCS/Bank topic, and the 2029 date plus the three CDP criteria (GNI, HAI, EVI) are the facts every later graduation story will build on.
stories.exam_facts: Khatun writes in Prothom Alo on 10 November 2026; the CDP reviews LDCs every three years on per-capita GNI, the Human Assets Index and the Economic and Environmental Vulnerability Index, requiring the thresholds in two consecutive reviews; the UN's 24 November 2021 resolution first fixed graduation at 24 November 2026 after a five-year preparatory period granted because of Covid-19; the latest extension also covers Nepal, and Laos received the same five-year preparatory period; Bangladesh has opened trade talks including an Economic Partnership Agreement with Japan; the columnist argues exporters need support on rules of origin, product certification, skills and finance.
stories.exam_relevance: LDC graduation, UN CDP criteria, trade preferences, rules of origin - core BCS/Bank economy topics.

stories.headline: Bangladesh, South Korea aim to finalise CEPA draft by December
stories.summary: Bangladesh and South Korea agreed on 10 November to finalise the draft of a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) by December, clearing the way for a formal signing ceremony. Commerce Minister Khandaker Abdul Muktadir and South Korean Ambassador Kim Ji-joon decided this at the Secretariat after Seoul sent its position on the draft with a detailed questionnaire; the minister also proposed joint shipbuilding investment and a Design and Development Centre using local engineers, while pledging priority help for Korean investors' operational and import difficulties.
stories.why_it_matters: CEPA would be Bangladesh's first major trade deal with a developed Asian economy as LDC graduation approaches in 2029, and South Korea is already a key investor, shipbuilder and LNG supplier.
stories.exam_facts: Meeting held 10 November 2026 at the Secretariat, Dhaka; the ambassador welcomed long-term technology transfer and joint investment with Hanwha Ocean and Hyundai Heavy Industries; LNG supplies were also discussed; Muktadir proposed the Design and Development Centre to use local engineers and skilled workers; the minister pledged government support to encourage greater South Korean investment; the two sides held extensive discussions on finalising the agreement and next steps.
stories.exam_relevance: Trade agreements, CEPA, LDC graduation, foreign investment - core BCS/Bank economy topics.
stories.key_people: Khandaker Abdul Muktadir, Commerce Minister; Kim Ji-joon, South Korean Ambassador to Bangladesh
stories.figures: Draft CEPA by December 2026; meeting 10 November 2026.

stories.headline: Tarique, Erdogan discuss defence, trade and Rohingya repatriation in Antalya
stories.summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan met in Antalya on 10 November - scheduled for 6:30pm but held at 7:15pm local time, according to UNB's outcome report - for about 30 minutes at the Maxx Royal Hotel, discussing defence cooperation, trade and investment, energy security and Rohingya repatriation. It was Tarique's second meeting with Erdogan since taking office, after their 22 September meeting in New York, and it caps a warming Dhaka-Ankara tie built on reciprocal foreign-minister visits and a joint defence and foreign-affairs committee.
stories.why_it_matters: The meeting is the clearest marker of the Dhaka-Ankara strategic turn since the BNP government took office, tying defence, trade and the Rohingya file together on the COP31 sidelines.
stories.exam_facts: Present: Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman and State Minister-1 for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir; topics also included joint investment in defence, mineral resources, renewable energy and climate change; Tarique thanked Turkiye for its support on the Rohingya issue at the International Court of Justice and sought continued backing at the UN and OIC for safe, dignified repatriation; Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan visited Dhaka in early June 2026; Army Chief General Waker-Uz-Zaman visited Turkiye in July 2026; Tarique is in Antalya 10-12 November for COP31 and delivers Bangladesh's statement on 12 November; no agreement was signed.
stories.exam_relevance: Foreign policy, defence cooperation, Rohingya repatriation, COP31 - core BCS current-affairs topics.
stories.key_people: Tarique Rahman, Prime Minister; Recep Tayyip Erdogan, President of Turkiye; Khalilur Rahman, Foreign Minister; Humaiun Kobir, State Minister-1 for Foreign Affairs

stories.headline: Poverty is rising again, and the dream is still to reduce it, economist says
stories.summary: Former World Bank lead economist Zahid Hussain tells Prothom Alo the economy is fragile: poverty, which Bangladesh once cut steadily, is now rising in both number and rate, growth is weakening, inflation stays high and real wages are falling with no significant rise in employment. He argues the next 10-15 years must deliver economic security above the poverty line - per-capita income up and inequality down together, through jobs, productivity and real wages - because people must not fall back below the line after illness or job loss.
stories.why_it_matters: Poverty and inequality are the spine of Bangladesh's development story for BCS/Bank, and Hussain's twin test - income up, inequality down - is the frame for every later jobs and wages story.
stories.exam_facts: Hussain spoke to Prothom Alo senior sub-editor Monzurul Islam; the interview was published 10 November 2026; he cites reports and surveys from the World Bank, IMF and PPRC; he points to the July 2024 uprising as proof people can organise against misrule and demand accountability; he notes life expectancy rose, poverty fell and industrialisation happened despite adversity, and agriculture now feeds far more than the 70 million people once worried over; 55 years after independence a significant share of the population remains poor or at risk of poverty.
stories.exam_relevance: Poverty, inequality, real wages, development economics - core BCS/Bank topics.
stories.key_people: Zahid Hussain, former lead economist, World Bank Dhaka office; Monzurul Islam, Prothom Alo senior sub-editor

stories.headline: Bangladesh Bank, Karmasangsthan Bank sign CIB agreement
stories.summary: Bangladesh Bank and Karmasangsthan Bank signed an agreement at the central bank's head office on 9 November giving Karmasangsthan Bank access to the Credit Information Bureau (CIB), so it can verify loan applicants' existing debts and repayment histories before lending. The check is meant to cut credit risk and defaults and raise transparency, because the bank lends to employment-seeking borrowers and must now see whether applicants already owe other banks or have repayment irregularities.
stories.why_it_matters: CIB checks are how Bangladesh Bank enforces lending discipline, and Karmasangsthan Bank's employment loans make its credit screening a direct Bank-exam topic.
stories.exam_facts: Signed by Bangladesh Bank CIB Director Md Shafiqul Islam and Karmasangsthan Bank Managing Director Arun Kumar Chowdhury; Deputy Governor Md Anis Ur Rahman attended as chief guest; executive director (Statistics-1) Ashish Kumar Roy chaired the ceremony; special guests included Shabnam Shirin, executive director (Statistics-2), Md Mojibur Rahman Sheikh and Muhammad Mahfuzur Rahman Khan; through the CIB the bank can identify repayment irregularities and assess applicants' overall debt obligations.
stories.exam_relevance: Banking, CIB, credit risk, loan defaults - core Bank-job topics.

stories.headline: Chattogram customs set for Tk1,686 crore overhaul with 15-storey complex
stories.summary: Chattogram Custom House, which handles about 90% of Bangladesh's international trade, is set for a Tk1,686 crore modernisation with a 15-storey office complex, advanced testing laboratories and a training academy, aiming to cut cargo clearance time by 25%. Operations are shifting to the World Trade Centre in Agrabad for three years - one of seven assessment groups moved on 1 November and the other six follow by the first week of December - while the old infrastructure is demolished.
stories.why_it_matters: Chattogram handles about 90% of Bangladesh's trade, so a 25% faster clearance there is the most concrete trade-facilitation number in this edition, and it feeds revenue and LDC-competitiveness questions.
stories.exam_facts: Project announced 10 November 2026; Chattogram is the country's largest revenue-collecting customs station; assistant commissioner Sharif Al Amin, the customs house spokesperson, said the temporary arrangement lasts three years; the project aims to make customs more technology-driven, transparent and efficient; automation aims to reduce inspections and traders' office visits.
stories.exam_relevance: Customs, trade facilitation, infrastructure, revenue - BCS/Bank economy topics.

stories.figures: Tk1,686 crore modernisation; 15-storey complex; 25% cut in clearance time; about 90% of international trade; 7 assessment groups; 3-year temporary arrangement.

stories.headline: BRAC Bank reports stellar performance in Q3
stories.summary: BRAC Bank's consolidated net profit after tax rose 38% year on year to Tk21.21 billion for the nine months to 30 September 2026, from Tk15.36 billion a year earlier, while standalone profit rose 50% to Tk15.84 billion from Tk10.55 billion. Managing Director Tareq Refat Ullah Khan credited diversified businesses, prudent governance and disciplined execution; deposits grew 16% and loans 7% since December 2025, and the cost-to-income ratio improved to 41% from 46%.
stories.why_it_matters: BRAC Bank is a bellwether private bank, and its 38% profit jump with a 41% cost-to-income ratio is the benchmark number for Bank-job questions on bank performance.
stories.exam_facts: Results presented at a virtual earnings call on Monday 9 November 2026; consolidated figures include all subsidiaries; the bank says it delivered growth well above the market while maintaining one of the industry's strongest asset quality indicators; Khan said the bank will stay focused on creating sustainable long-term value for customers, shareholders and the economy; the press statement stressed productivity, cost discipline and digital transformation.
stories.exam_relevance: Bank earnings, NPAT, cost-to-income ratio, asset quality - core Bank-job topics.

stories.headline: Dollar rate crosses Tk125 as fuel import payments rise
stories.summary: The dollar rate for remittance purchases through banking channels crossed Tk125 on 10 November, with banks buying dollars from exchange houses at Tk125.10-125.15, up more than Tk2.30 in three months, while letters of credit settled at Tk124.90-124.97. Bangladesh Bank officials and bankers attribute the pressure mainly to fuel import payments: BPC now imports at about $148 a barrel against under $90 before the March Middle East war, and needs about $800 million for November payments, after the central bank sold $122 million from reserves last week.
stories.why_it_matters: The taka's slide past Tk125 ties the exchange rate directly to fuel imports and reserves, the exact chain - war, oil price, import bill, reserves - that BCS/Bank questions test.
stories.exam_facts: Overall import expenditure rose 15% in the first quarter of FY26 (July-September); petroleum import costs rose 27.87% to $2.98 billion from $2.33 billion a year earlier; petroleum, oil and lubricant imports surged 103% to $3.71 billion from $1.82 billion; remittances reached $30.80 billion in the first 10 months of 2026, exports $41.09 billion and imports $64.95 billion; between July and 9 November remittances totalled $12.75 billion, up from $11.12 billion a year earlier; Petrobangla also faces substantial import payment obligations this month.
stories.exam_relevance: Exchange rate, foreign reserves, fuel imports, remittance - core BCS/Bank economy topics.
stories.key_people: Bangladesh Bank; Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation (BPC); Petrobangla

stories.headline: Financial inclusion reaches 64.5% of adults, but students' and farmers' savings decline
stories.summary: About 64.5% of Bangladeshi adults now have access to formal financial services, Bangladesh Bank's Financial Inclusion Report 2025 says, but the gains are uneven: deposits in school banking accounts fell 3.69% and savings in special Tk10 farmer accounts fell 8.77% in 2025, even as mobile financial services and agent banking grew strongly. School accounts rose 8.57% to 47.55 lakh by December 2025, yet their deposits fell to Tk1,994 crore from Tk2,071 crore, while MFS transactions jumped 25.58% to more than Tk21.83 lakh crore.
stories.why_it_matters: The 64.5% inclusion figure is the headline Bank-exam number, and the split - accounts up, savings down - is the nuance that separates a memorised figure from an understood one.
stories.exam_facts: The report reviews banking, MFS, microfinance, capital market and insurance during 2024 and 2025; school accounts numbered 43.80 lakh a year earlier; more than half (52.24%) of school accounts were rural, though urban accounts held 70.29% of deposits; boys held 54.9% of school deposits and girls 45.1%; the school programme aims to bring students into formal banking early; Tk10 accounts were introduced for marginal farmers and low-income people.
stories.exam_relevance: Financial inclusion, MFS, agent banking, school banking - core Bank-job topics.
stories.figures: 64.5% of adults included; school deposits down 3.69%, Tk10 accounts down 8.77%; school accounts 47.55 lakh, up 8.57%; deposits Tk1,994 crore vs Tk2,071 crore; MFS transactions up 25.58% to Tk21.83 lakh crore.

stories.headline: Fish export earnings to reach $1b by 2030: Minister
stories.summary: Bangladesh aims to raise annual fish and fish-product export earnings to US$1 billion by 2030, up from about $500 million in 2026, Fisheries and Livestock Minister Mohammad Amin Ur Rashid told Parliament on 10 November. The Department of Fisheries has a five-year action plan under the government's election manifesto; earnings were $504.58 million (about Tk6,193 crore) from 93,530 tonnes in 2025-26, against $501 million from 90,620 tonnes in FY25, with the EU the largest destination among 52-plus countries.
stories.why_it_matters: A $1 billion-by-2030 export target with a five-year plan is a ready-made BCS/Bank question, and fisheries is one of the few export lines still growing while total exports slipped.
stories.exam_facts: The minister replied in writing to BNP MP Md Mustafizur Rahman Babul of Jamalpur-3; overall merchandise exports fell slightly from $48.28 billion in FY25 to $48 billion in FY26, while fisheries' share rose from 1.04% to 1.05%; figures come from the Export Promotion Bureau and Bangladesh Bank; the sector kept positive export growth despite the global slowdown and unfavourable international markets.
stories.exam_relevance: Exports, fisheries, five-year plan, EPB data - BCS/Bank economy topics.
stories.key_people: Mohammad Amin Ur Rashid, Fisheries and Livestock Minister; Md Mustafizur Rahman Babul, MP, Jamalpur-3
stories.figures: Target US$1 billion by 2030 from about $500 million in 2026; 2025-26: $504.58 million, 93,530 tonnes; FY25: $501 million, 90,620 tonnes; exports to 52+ countries; fisheries 1.05% of total exports.

stories.headline: Sharif Uddin gets ACC job back with seniority
stories.summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission has withdrawn its 16 February 2022 order dismissing assistant director Md Sharif Uddin and reinstated him with seniority and all outstanding salaries and allowances, under a notification issued on 10 November. Sharif was dismissed after investigating land-acquisition irregularities in Patuakhali and filing a general diary over death threats; he challenged Rule 54(2) - dismissal without a show-cause chance - in a writ in March 2022, and the Appellate Division's December 2023 verdict kept the rule but ordered 12 safeguards.
stories.why_it_matters: Rule 54(2) - dismissal without show cause - is a classic BCS question on service rules, and Sharif's reinstatement with seniority is the case that shows how the courts fenced it with 12 safeguards.
stories.exam_facts: Before Patuakhali (from 16 June 2021) Sharif worked at the ACC's Chattogram office; his dismissal sparked protests, including a human chain by ACC employees at headquarters; the High Court adjourned his writ on 25 May 2022 pending the ACC's appeal in the Md Ahsan Ali case; on 16 March 2023 the Appellate Division allowed the ACC's appeal, setting aside the High Court ruling that had invalidated Rule 54(2); the High Court issued a rule on 6 February 2024 and delivered its verdict on 9 July 2025; the dismissal order gave 90 days' salary and applicable benefits.
stories.exam_relevance: ACC, service rules, writ petitions, Appellate Division - core BCS topics.
stories.key_people: Md Sharif Uddin, Assistant Director, ACC; Md Ahsan Ali, ACC official
stories.figures: Dismissed 16 February 2022; reinstated 10 November 2026; Rule 54(2) of ACC (Employees) Service Rules, 2008; 12 observations/guidelines; 90 days' salary in dismissal order.

stories.headline: 146 RMG factories suspend work as fresh unrest hits Ashulia and Gazipur
stories.summary: About 146 garment factories suspended production and declared holidays on 10 November as fresh labour unrest hit Ashulia and Gazipur, despite the wage board's work and an agreement that the revised minimum wage takes effect in December. Over 100 affected factories are in Ashulia and at least 30 in Gazipur; workers entered factories but did not join production, some factories were vandalised, two workers were injured in a clash with police, and owners may now decide on indefinite closure under section 13(1).
stories.why_it_matters: RMG is Bangladesh's biggest export earner, so a 146-factory stoppage during an agreed wage-board process - with section 13(1) closure on the table - is the labour-economy question of the week.
stories.exam_facts: The BGMEA list named 146 factories, with 108 names available; factories of Islam Group, Starling, Envoy, Knit Asia and Mondol Group in Ashulia were unable to continue production; the Department of Inspection for Factories and Establishments (DIFE) confirmed the Gazipur holidays through deputy inspector general MM Mamun-Ur-Rashid; BGMEA vice-president Shehab Udduza Chowdhury said talks had been progressing smoothly since the wage board was formed; the workers' side proposed a Tk32,000 minimum wage; unrest has run for nearly two weeks.
stories.exam_relevance: RMG, minimum wage, labour unrest, BGMEA, section 13(1) - recurring BCS/Bank economy topics.
stories.key_people: Mahmud Hasan Khan Babu, BGMEA President; Shehab Udduza Chowdhury, BGMEA Vice-President; MM Mamun-Ur-Rashid, Deputy Inspector General, DIFE
stories.figures: 146 factories suspended; 100+ in Ashulia; at least 30 in Gazipur; 108 names on BGMEA list; 2 workers injured; new wage from December 2026; workers propose Tk32,000 minimum wage.

stories.headline: Revenue shortfall crosses Tk50,000 crore in first four months of FY27
stories.summary: The National Board of Revenue collected under Tk1.28 lakh crore in July-October 2026, against a target of about Tk1.78 lakh crore - a shortfall of more than Tk50,000 crore in the first four months of FY27, after a Tk43,000 crore gap in the first quarter alone. Sluggish activity and weak VAT receipts are blamed: income and import taxes grew about 14% but VAT fell about 6% year on year, while overall growth stayed below 6% against over 16% a year earlier, leaving the annual target increasingly out of reach.
stories.why_it_matters: A Tk50,000 crore revenue gap in four months is the fiscal number behind every budget and deficit question, and the VAT fall against 14% income-tax growth shows exactly where collection is breaking down.
stories.exam_facts: Figures are preliminary NBR estimates reported 11 November 2026; economists and NBR officials blame subdued activity, an overly ambitious revenue target and policy challenges; a senior NBR official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the high growth target made the gap particularly pronounced; revenue in the first four months was higher than the same period last year, but growth stayed below 6% against more than 16% last year.
stories.exam_relevance: NBR, revenue collection, VAT, fiscal policy - core BCS/Bank economy topics.
stories.figures: Collected under Tk1.28 lakh crore vs target about Tk1.78 lakh crore; shortfall over Tk50,000 crore; Tk43,000 crore after Q1; income and import tax up about 14%, VAT down about 6%; growth under 6% vs over 16% last year.

stories.headline: CAAB board approves draft deal with Japanese consortium to run Dhaka airport's third terminal
stories.summary: The Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh board on 10 November approved the draft agreement with a Japanese consortium to operate Dhaka airport's Third Terminal, a mandatory step before signing that now goes to the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism and other ministries. TBS reports the draft bars any new competing civilian airport within 100 km of Dhaka from opening for 15 years - but the Caab source declined to confirm it, saying details will come at a press conference, so the condition is reported, not confirmed.
stories.why_it_matters: Who runs the Third Terminal - and on what reported terms - is the infrastructure question that links aviation, foreign investment and competition policy, and the unconfirmed 100 km clause is exactly the detail an exam could probe.
stories.exam_facts: Caab Chairman Air Vice Marshal Md Mostafa Mahmood Siddiq presided over the 10 November board meeting; the board reviewed the proposed terms and conditions in detail; a source who attended the meeting told The Business Standard, requesting anonymity, that board approval was a mandatory step before signing; the preliminary decision to hand the terminal and ground handling to the Japanese consortium had already drawn criticism over concessions reportedly offered; the draft deal now awaits approval from the relevant ministries.
stories.exam_relevance: Aviation, PPP, concessions, infrastructure - BCS/Bank topics.
stories.key_people: Air Vice Marshal Md Mostafa Mahmood Siddiq, Chairman, Caab

phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: on the sidelines of a conference/summit; a meeting on the sidelines
phrases.Article headline: Tarique-Erdogan meeting in Antalya today as Dhaka-Ankara ties grow closer
phrases.Exam value: High-frequency diplomatic idiom in BCS/Bank current-affairs passages.

phrases.English explanation: In connection with what has just been discussed; given this situation.
phrases.Original example 1: In this context, trade agreements can play a pivotal role.
phrases.Original example 2: In this context, on 25 May 2022, the High Court adjourned the hearing of Sharif's writ petition challenging the legality of dismissal under Rule 54(2) until the disposal of the ACC's appeal.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: in this context, ...; in that context
phrases.Article headline: Economy and reforms: LDC graduation window extended, challenges remain
phrases.Exam value: Common linking phrase in editorials and formal essays.

phrases.English explanation: According to; in accordance with a rule, resolution or order.
phrases.Original example 1: As per the UN General Assembly resolution of 24 November 2021, Bangladesh's graduation date was initially fixed for 24 November 2026.
phrases.Original example 2: As per the rules, he will be entitled to his seniority and all outstanding salaries and allowances.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: as per the rules; as per the resolution; as per the agreement
phrases.Article headline: Economy and reforms: LDC graduation window extended, challenges remain
phrases.Exam value: Standard formal phrase in legal and official passages.

phrases.English explanation: Having risen from a lower earlier figure to a higher one.
phrases.Original example 1: On a standalone basis, NPAT rose 50% year-on-year to Tk 15.84 billion, up from Tk 10.55 billion a year earlier.
phrases.Original example 2: Between July and 9 November, remittances totalled $12.75 billion, up from $11.12 billion a year earlier.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: up from $X; up from last year; rose to X, up from Y
phrases.Article headline: BRAC Bank reports stellar performance in Q3
phrases.Exam value: Key data-comparison phrase in economics passages.

phrases.Original example 1: He said Seoul had already communicated its position on the draft agreement to Bangladesh, along with a detailed questionnaire.
phrases.Original example 2: Along with this observation, the ACC was asked to follow 12 observations or guidelines when applying the provision.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: along with a detailed...; along with this observation
phrases.Article headline: Bangladesh, South Korea aim to finalise CEPA draft by December
phrases.Exam value: Common connector phrase in formal passages.

phrases.English explanation: During the first three months of a financial year or period.
phrases.Original example 1: Central bank data show overall import expenditure rose 15% in the first quarter of FY26 (July-September), while petroleum import costs increased 27.87% to $2.98 billion from $2.33 billion a year earlier.
phrases.Original example 2: The shortfall had already reached around Tk43,000 crore in the first quarter, from July to September, according to NBR sources.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: in the first quarter of FY26; in the first quarter, from July to September
phrases.Article headline: Dollar rate crosses Tk125 as fuel import payments rise
phrases.Exam value: Standard fiscal-calendar phrase in economics passages.

phrases.English explanation: A smaller amount or number than the one stated.
phrases.Original example 1: Since the Middle East war broke out in March, fuel prices have surged, with the Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation (BPC) now importing fuel at around $148 per barrel, against less than $90 before the war.
phrases.Original example 2: According to preliminary NBR estimates, the revenue authority collected less than Tk1.28 lakh crore between July and October, against a target of around Tk1.78 lakh crore.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: less than $X; less than Tk...; collected less than...
phrases.Article headline: Dollar rate crosses Tk125 as fuel import payments rise
phrases.Exam value: Basic quantifier phrase; essential for reading data correctly.

phrases.English explanation: A larger amount or number than the one stated.
phrases.Original example 1: At the meeting in New York, Erdogan praised Bangladesh for sheltering more than one million Rohingya.
phrases.Original example 2: The rate has risen by more than Tk2.30 in three months, while letters of credit (LCs) were settled at Tk124.90-124.97 per dollar.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: more than one million; more than Tk...; more than X in three months
phrases.Article headline: Tarique-Erdogan meeting in Antalya today as Dhaka-Ankara ties grow closer
phrases.Exam value: Basic quantifier phrase; essential for reading data correctly.

phrases.English explanation: The first four months of a financial year or period.
phrases.Original example 1: The National Board of Revenue (NBR) has fallen more than Tk50,000 crore short of its revenue collection target in the first four months of the 2026-27 financial year, as sluggish economic activity and weak VAT receipts continue to weigh on tax collection despite government efforts to boost revenue.
phrases.Original example 2: Although revenue collection during the first four months was higher than in the corresponding period of the previous financial year, growth remained below 6%.
phrases.Common collocations / grammar pattern: in the first four months of FY27; during the first four months of the year
phrases.Article headline: Revenue shortfall exceeds Tk50,000cr in first four months of FY27
phrases.Exam value: Standard fiscal-period phrase in revenue and budget passages.

mcqs.question: The word 'prohibitive' most nearly means —
mcqs.explanation: Prohibitive costs are so high they prevent action; Khatun says prohibitive power, energy and customs costs stop businesses cutting production costs.

mcqs.question: A 'questionnaire' is —
mcqs.explanation: A questionnaire is a set of written questions; Seoul sent its position on the CEPA draft along with a detailed questionnaire.

mcqs.question: The word 'reciprocal' most nearly means —
mcqs.explanation: Reciprocal means given or exchanged between two sides; Dhaka-Ankara ties grew through reciprocal foreign-minister visits.

mcqs.question: A 'precedent' is —

options.C: a past case as a guide

mcqs.explanation: A precedent is an earlier event used as a guide; Hussain says the July 2024 uprising set a real precedent for demanding accountability.

mcqs.question: In banking, 'obligations' most nearly means —
mcqs.explanation: Obligations are debts or duties owed; the CIB lets the bank assess applicants' overall debt obligations.

mcqs.question: 'Relocate' most nearly means —

options.B: to move to a new place

mcqs.explanation: Relocate means to move to a new place; the remaining six customs groups are expected to relocate by the first week of December.

mcqs.question: 'Prudent' most nearly means —
mcqs.explanation: Prudent means careful and wise; BRAC Bank's CEO credited prudent governance for the strong Q3 results.

mcqs.question: When a currency 'depreciates', it —
mcqs.explanation: Depreciate means to lose value; the taka continues to depreciate as the dollar crossed Tk125.

mcqs.question: 'Uneven' progress most nearly means progress that is —
mcqs.explanation: Uneven means not equal or balanced; inclusion reached 64.5% but progress was uneven for students and farmers.

mcqs.question: An election 'manifesto' is —

options.A: a voting booth at a centre
options.C: a campaign rally in a town

mcqs.explanation: A manifesto is a public declaration of policies; the fisheries five-year plan implements the government's election manifesto.

mcqs.question: The phrase 'on the sidelines of the conference' means —
mcqs.explanation: On the sidelines means at meetings held alongside a main event; Tarique was to hold bilateral meetings on the sidelines of COP31.

mcqs.question: In 'compared with Tk15.36 billion', 'compared with' is used to —
mcqs.explanation: Compared with sets one figure against another; BRAC Bank's Tk21.21 billion NPAT is given compared with Tk15.36 billion a year earlier.

mcqs.question: Bangladesh will now graduate from the LDC category on —
mcqs.explanation: The UN General Assembly's 29 October decision moved graduation from 24 November 2026 to 24 November 2029.

mcqs.question: Bangladesh and South Korea aim to finalise the CEPA draft by —
mcqs.explanation: The two sides agreed on 10 November to finalise the CEPA draft by December, clearing the way for a signing ceremony.

mcqs.question: According to the UNB outcome report, the Tarique-Erdogan meeting began at —
mcqs.explanation: The meeting was scheduled for 6:30pm, but UNB's outcome report says it began at 7:15pm local time and lasted about 30 minutes.

mcqs.question: The CIB agreement lets Karmasangsthan Bank check an applicant's —
mcqs.explanation: Through the CIB the bank can check existing debts and repayment histories before lending, to cut credit risk and defaults.

mcqs.question: The Chattogram customs modernisation aims to cut cargo clearance time by —
mcqs.explanation: The Tk1,686 crore modernisation aims to cut cargo clearance time by 25%, with a 15-storey complex and testing labs.

mcqs.question: BRAC Bank's consolidated NPAT for the nine months to 30 September 2026 was —
mcqs.explanation: Consolidated NPAT rose 38% to Tk21.21 billion; Tk15.84 billion was the standalone figure and Tk15.36 billion last year's consolidated figure.

mcqs.question: On 10 November banks bought dollars from exchange houses at —
mcqs.explanation: Banks bought dollars at Tk125.10-125.15; Tk124.90-124.97 was the LC settlement rate and $148 the oil price per barrel.

mcqs.question: According to Bangladesh Bank's Financial Inclusion Report 2025, about what share of adults has access to formal financial services?
mcqs.explanation: About 64.5% of adults have access; 52.24% is the rural share of school accounts and 70.29% the urban share of school deposits.

mcqs.question: Bangladesh aims to raise fish export earnings to US$1 billion by —
mcqs.explanation: The minister told Parliament the target is US$1 billion by 2030, up from about $500 million in 2026.

mcqs.question: Sharif Uddin was reinstated with seniority after the ACC withdrew its dismissal order of —
mcqs.explanation: The ACC dismissed Sharif Uddin on 16 February 2022 and withdrew that order on 10 November 2026, reinstating him with seniority.

mcqs.question: How many garment factories suspended production on 10 November?
mcqs.explanation: About 146 factories suspended production; 108 is the number of names available on the BGMEA list and 30 the Gazipur count.

mcqs.question: The NBR's revenue shortfall in the first four months of FY27 was more than —
mcqs.explanation: The shortfall was more than Tk50,000 crore; Tk43,000 crore was the gap after the first quarter and Tk1.28 lakh crore the amount collected.

mcqs.question: The reported condition in the Third Terminal draft deal would bar a competing civilian airport within 100 km of Dhaka for —
mcqs.explanation: TBS reports the draft includes a condition barring a competing airport within 100 km for 15 years, but the Caab source declined to confirm it, so it is reported, not confirmed.
